abstraction_design.rationale: Abstractions map well onto real variation and an Items section could reuse almost all of them; the cost is that the home page and team page couldn't reuse the card pipeline, and pokeapi.ts mixes cache client, error mapping, display helpers and domain mappers in one file.

findings.issue: Card construction (id/name/sprite URL) is implemented three times: cardsFor (server/utils/pokeapi.ts:100-112), the home page's cards computed (index.vue:43-52), and team.get.ts:30-36; the home page synthesizes the sprite URL inline, so a sprite fix covers only 4 of 5 card lists.
findings.suggestion: Have /api/species and /api/team return the same Card shape built by one helper in server/utils (reading sprites from the Pokémon record's sprites.front_default rather than constructing the URL), and make the sprite logic live in exactly one place.

findings.issue: Server payload shapes are hand-duplicated in pages with no shared types — the card/member shape is declared ~8 times (pokeapi.ts:88, CardList.vue:2, PokemonCard.vue:1, moves/[name].vue:5, abilities/[name].vue:6, types/[name].vue:5, team.vue:2 vs team.get.ts:1), so payload changes require parallel edits and drift is invisible to TypeScript.
findings.suggestion: Use Nuxt 4's shared/types/ (auto-imported in both app and server) for Card, ChainNode, MoveRow and each page's data shape — or lean on typed server routes' inferred useFetch response types.

findings.issue: humanize is duplicated verbatim in the app (composables/format.ts:1-5) and the server (server/utils/pokeapi.ts:39-42); a display-rule fix (e.g. keeping periods in 'Mr. Mime') must be made twice.
findings.suggestion: Move humanize (and any other context-free helpers) to shared/utils/, which Nuxt 4 auto-imports into both the Vue app and Nitro server.

findings.issue: The page re-derives the API base from runtime config and hard-codes the /media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png path, duplicating knowledge that belongs to the server layer (pokeapi.ts:7,54).
findings.suggestion: Return sprite URLs (or the full Card shape) from /api/species so the client never knows about API/media internals.

findings.issue: usePageData maps every server error to a 404 'Not found' page (error.value?.statusCode ?? 404), so a 500 from the internal API or upstream PokeAPI is silently presented as Not found, hiding real bugs.
findings.suggestion: Only coerce to 404 when statusCode is 404; pass other statuses through so error.vue can distinguish them.

findings.issue: The file is a grab-bag: fetch client + cache + NotFound plumbing (1-63) alongside display helpers (humanize/englishName/latestFlavorText) and domain mappers (allTypes/cardsFor/speciesNames).
findings.suggestion: Split into a thin api-client (fetch/cache/NotFound) and a pokemon-shaping module; that also makes the data-source change scenario a one-file edit.

findings.issue: Types are exported from SFCs (MoveRow from components/MovesTable.vue, ChainNode from components/EvolutionNode.vue) and imported into pages, coupling pages to component internals for types.
findings.suggestion: Declare shared row/node types in shared/types/ (or app/types/) and have the components consume them.

findings.issue: useFetch with a static key computed from the initial team (`team:${names.value}`) combined with a reactive query and watch:[team] is subtle — the key no longer matches the data after any team change.
findings.suggestion: Drop the explicit key and let Nuxt auto-generate it from the reactive URL/options, keeping only the reactive query + watch.

findings.issue: All styling is centralized in one 600-line global stylesheet, so components aren't stylistically self-contained (restyling PokemonCard means editing main.css, not the component); it is, however, clearly sectioned with comments, which keeps it findable.
findings.suggestion: Consider scoped styles in the small presentational components (TypeBadge, PokemonCard, PageSection) while keeping the layout/section CSS global.

summary: A small, idiomatic Nuxt 4 app with a genuinely clean server/client seam: pages consume typed internal /api routes, all PokeAPI and caching knowledge is confined to one server module, and features are directory-shaped so they delete easily. The recurring weakness is duplication along the card/sprite pipeline — three separate card-construction sites, a client-side copy of the API/media URL logic, humanize in two files, and ~8 hand-written declarations of the same payload shape with no shared/types. Fixing that one axis would move this from good to exemplary.
